newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moldova's rebel region to hold own poll.
newsitem.headline: Moldova's rebel region to hold own poll.

text.p: Moldova's breakaway Dnestr region has decided to elect its own leader on December 22, just over a month after a national presidential poll on November 17, the head of the regional parliament said on Friday.
"We are going to hold presidential elections on December 22 rather than on November 17, when Moldova elects its own head of state," Grigory Marakutsa told Reuters from the regional capital Tiraspol.

Dnestr leader Igor Smirnov, the former director of a big electrical firm in the region, is likely to be the strongest candidate in the regional election. Moldovan President Mircea Snegur will seek re-election in the national poll.
Marakutsa said Dnestr authorities would not allow Moldovan polling stations in the region on November 17 but they would not prevent anyone wishing to vote outside the region from doing so.

The industrialised Dnestr region broke away from Moldova in 1990, fearing that its mostly Slav residents could become second-rate citizens if Moldova chooses to merge with ethnic kin in Romania. Chisinau has since abandoned such merger plans.
Hundreds of people were killed in a war between Moldovan security forces and Dnestr rebels in 1992.
Talks on Dnestr's future status have stalled on Dnestr demands to be recognised as an independent state.
